messages:
Maria (CEO): quick sticky from today's all-hands 1 two asks: a tight press-friendly one-liner about what we do, and guidance on how public our model perf numbers should be. short replies pls.
Ajay (CTO): one-liner idea: "runtime + ops for production LLMs." technical guidance: publish vetted ranges with the test config alongside any numbers. no single-number claims.
Lena (Head Product): for marketing, keep the press line <= 6 words. GTM should have separate hero messages for PLG vs enterprise. make verified-models public, BYOM labeled experimental.
Tom (Sales): field note: compliance and SLA details come up earlier than teams expect. Sales needs a 1-pager: SLA + compliance facts for demos.
Priya (Eng): engineering note: whenever we publish latency/cost, include the sequence length, batch, and hw used. BYOM needs a minimal runbook (quant, mem, sharding). ops-bot: weekly perf exports live at /dashboards/perf-summary.
Sam (Research): competitor quick map: clouds = scale but opaque pricing; low-cost inference vendors = aggressive quant but limited SLAs; OSS runtimes = flexible but ops-heavy. highlight rollouts, observability, and fallback behavior as our differentiators.
Darci (Strategy): tagline tests to run: A) "Inference you can rely on." B) "Predictable inference, every deployment." will queue A/B on site and newsletter.
Maria (CEO): thanks. who volunteers to own the verified-model page and benchmark cadence?
Ajay (CTO): happy to own the tech appendix for benchmarks and review wording.
Priya (Eng): I'll draft the BYOM runbook and post in #eng.
Tom (Sales): I'll push the SLA/compliance 1-pager with GTM.
Darci (Strategy): i'll schedule a quarterly cadence for model reviews and own the rubric.
Maria (CEO): perfect. i'll assemble a tiny README and circulate drafts for review. closing this thread 1 post updates in comments if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
